scientific_queries.note: Audit of R94's identity-stability statistic before letting it into the synthesis.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round audits its own predecessor and retracts the interpretation rather than adding to it.
the_flaw_in_R94: R94 compared top-5 sets across draws that used different masks, i.e. different available drugs, so the sets had to change; that measures input sensitivity, not ranking stability

decisions.H245_note: false at full coverage, where masks barely alter the leading drugs and R94's method is therefore optimistic; true at 36% and 16%, which is where the claim was made

corrected_reading.reproducibility_given_fixed_information: top-5 overlap 0.836 / 0.820 / 0.757 at full, 36% and 16% coverage, with no significant decay
corrected_reading.what_R94_measured: the effect of changing which drugs are available, which is not irreproducibility
corrected_reading.what_survives_from_R94: the hit rate under fixed information still falls 12.20% -> 9.49% -> 8.32%, so the mild coverage cost stands

methodological_lesson: R93 and R94 make the same mistake: treating a quantity fixed by the construction as a finding. Before reporting any stability or sensitivity statistic, ask what else changed in that comparison.
limits: bootstrapping keys double-counts, so marginal variance is understated and the overlap rates are optimistic
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI

register_updates.C68: new correction: R94's irreproducibility reading is retracted
